key_insight: An adaptive simulated annealing search can discover moderately sized quantum error-correcting CSS and SWEL codes with high rates and unusually large distances, including codes that support transversal logical gates.
engineering_relevance: The result provides practical seed codes for fault-tolerant quantum architectures and near-term hardware demonstrations, especially where high-rate encoding and gate-friendly code structure matter.
method: Adaptive simulated annealing over stabilizer-code search space
Energy surrogate combines code distance with number of minimum-weight logical operators
Targets CSS codes and SWEL codes with transversal Hadamard and phase gates
evidence_signal: For block lengths up to 50 physical qubits, the search finds state-of-the-art CSS and SWEL codes whose distances often meet or exceed quantum Gilbert-Varshamov bound variants.
watch_item: The search objective is a surrogate for code-capacity logical error rate, so real hardware performance may differ under circuit-level noise and implementation constraints.
